originalTitle: Will Google be Berkshire CEO Greg Abel's best stock pick after predecessor Warren Buffett's Apple bet?
simplifiedContent: Berkshire Hathaway, a big investment company, has a new CEO named Greg Abel who started in January. He's using the company's large amount of cash, nearly $400 billion, to make new investments. One of the main companies he's investing in is Alphabet, which is the parent company of Google. This is a significant move because it shows a change in the company's investment strategy under the new CEO. It will be interesting to see if this investment pays off, especially since the previous CEO, Warren Buffett, had a successful investment in Apple.

originalTitle: TCS, HDFC Bank, 8 others with up to 49% upside. How many in your portfolio?
simplifiedContent: A financial company has identified 10 well-established companies, including TCS and HDFC Bank, that they think are good investments. This means that if you invest in these companies, you could potentially earn a return of up to 49% on your investment. This information may be useful for individual investors looking to add new stocks to their portfolio.

originalTitle: 5 world market themes for the week ahead
simplifiedContent: This week, investors will be watching several important events that can affect the stock market. One key event is the release of earnings from TSMC, a company that makes chips for artificial intelligence, which will give us an idea of how much demand there is for these chips. We'll also see big banks in the US release their profits, which are expected to be strong. Additionally, investors will be keeping an eye on oil prices, US inflation data, and China's economic growth, all of which can influence the market. These events can help investors understand what might happen to interest rates and the overall economy, which is why they matter.

originalTitle: Greed and Fear report: Christopher Wood sees 'AI fatigue' setting in. Why Jefferies is turning bullish on India
simplifiedContent: A financial expert named Christopher Wood from a company called Jefferies thinks that investors are getting tired of stocks related to Artificial Intelligence (AI) and are losing interest. This is being called "AI fatigue". As a result, Jefferies is becoming more positive about investing in India's stock market, which they think is undervalued, meaning its stocks are not as expensive as they could be. Wood and Jefferies still believe that AI will be important in the long term, especially for companies that make memory chips. They are shifting their focus to India's market because they think it's a better value than the currently popular AI stocks.

originalTitle: Buy or sell: Sumeet Bagadia recommends three stocks to buy on Monday - 13 July 2026
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the news item: The Indian stock market had a good day on July 10, with two important measures, Sensex and Nifty 50, increasing by 1.08% and 1.02% respectively. This happened because companies recently released strong earnings reports, which made investors feel more confident. Some good news from outside India also helped boost investor confidence. Despite this, the market didn't do as well as it had in the previous four weeks, but it's still looking positive. This matters because it can affect how people decide to invest their money on Monday, July 13.

originalTitle: Three PSU stocks with strong expansion plans
simplifiedContent: There are three stocks from government-owned companies that are planning to expand their businesses. These companies, known as Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), have a lot of orders to fulfill, which is a good sign for their growth. This means they have a strong foundation for future success. It's worth paying attention to these stocks because of their potential for growth and increasing demand for their services. The fact that they have a growing order book suggests that they have a steady stream of work coming in, which could lead to increased profits.
